questions.q: In a Hadith, God says on the Last Day: “I was ill, but you did not come to nurse Me.” What principle does the article draw from it?
options: That only the sick deserve care
Not quite. The article says: Whoever wishes to find God must serve those in need – there he would have found Him.
That worship alone is enough
Not quite. The article says: Whoever wishes to find God must serve those in need – there he would have found Him.
That God shares human weakness
Not quite. The article says: Whoever wishes to find God must serve those in need – there he would have found Him.
Whoever wishes to find God must serve those in need – there he would have found Him
Yes. Worship of God and service to man go together.
questions.rationale: “Such and such servant of Mine was ill. Had you gone there, you would have found Me there with him.”

questions.q: How does the article describe the act of helping another person with what one has?
options: As a duty only of the wealthy
Not quite. The article says: As a way of thanking God for the blessings He has given.
As a way of thanking God for the blessings He has given
Right. The helper has been given more, and spends it in God’s path.
As a loan to be repaid later
Not quite. The article says: As a way of thanking God for the blessings He has given.
As a favour that earns influence
Not quite. The article says: As a way of thanking God for the blessings He has given.
questions.rationale: “On all such occasions when one man helps out another by virtue of those blessings which God has given him, he is in fact showing his gratitude to God for these favours.”

questions.q: What does the article mean by observing silence?
options: Not merely being quiet, but contemplating – which opens the door to God-realization
Well read. “My silence should be silent contemplation.”
Living alone, away from people
Not quite. The article says: Not merely being quiet, but contemplating – which opens the door to God-realization.
Refusing to answer questions
Not quite. The article says: Not merely being quiet, but contemplating – which opens the door to God-realization.
Speaking only on fixed days
Not quite. The article says: Not merely being quiet, but contemplating – which opens the door to God-realization.
questions.rationale: “Observing silence is not only to remain quiet but it means to contemplate… Silence is the door to Ma’rifat.”

questions.q: What kind of unity did the Prophet’s Companions have, according to the article?
options: Unity imposed by strict rules
Not quite. The article says: Unity despite real differences – they were one on the central cause.
Unity because they never disagreed
Not quite. The article says: Unity despite real differences – they were one on the central cause.
Unity only within each family
Not quite. The article says: Unity despite real differences – they were one on the central cause.
Unity despite real differences – they were one on the central cause
Yes. Unity does not require sameness.
questions.rationale: “Their unity was not of the sort that recognized no differences… in spite of all such personal differences, they were united on the central cause.”

questions.q: What does the article call the bedrock of collective unity?
options: Constant meetings and speeches
Not quite. The article says: Individual sacrifice – stepping aside, recognising others’ merit, accepting their opinion.
Equal wealth for everyone
Not quite. The article says: Individual sacrifice – stepping aside, recognising others’ merit, accepting their opinion.
Individual sacrifice – stepping aside, recognising others’ merit, accepting their opinion
Correct. And a great common purpose ends petty disputes.
A strong and feared leader
Not quite. The article says: Individual sacrifice – stepping aside, recognising others’ merit, accepting their opinion.
questions.rationale: “It means offering the best seat to another, standing aside while others forge ahead… Such individual sacrifice is the bedrock of collective unity.”

questions.q: Asked what faith means, how did the Prophet reply?
options: “Strength and courage”
Not quite. The article says: “Self-restraint and gentleness”.
“Knowledge and argument”
Not quite. The article says: “Self-restraint and gentleness”.
“Wealth and generosity”
Not quite. The article says: “Self-restraint and gentleness”.
“Self-restraint and gentleness”
Right. Faith shows in character.
questions.rationale: “When the Prophet Muhammad was asked by ‘Amr ibn ‘Abasah what was meant by faith, he replied, ‘Self-restraint and gentleness.’”

questions.q: What does the Prophet teach about a trust placed in your care by someone who has himself let you down?
options: Keep it as compensation
Not quite. The article says: Return it faithfully all the same – never betray a trust.
Return it faithfully all the same – never betray a trust
Yes. Another’s failing does not excuse one’s own.
Hand it to a third person
Not quite. The article says: Return it faithfully all the same – never betray a trust.
Return half of it
Not quite. The article says: Return it faithfully all the same – never betray a trust.
questions.rationale: “Never betray anyone’s trust, not even if the person concerned has failed to stand by his commitments to you.”

questions.q: The Prophet stood up as a funeral passed, and was told it was that of a Jew. What did he answer?
options: “Then let us sit”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
“Was he not a human being?”
Exactly. Every person is worthy of respect.
“I did not know”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
“Who were his family?”
Not quite. The article says: “Was he not a human being?”.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet replied: ‘Was he not a human being?’ This tells us that every human being is worthy of respect.”

questions.q: What did the Madinah Charter lay down for the different groups living in the city?
options: Only the largest group would be consulted
Not quite. The article says: Each group’s affairs would be decided according to its own religious tradition.
All groups would follow one common law
Not quite. The article says: Each group’s affairs would be decided according to its own religious tradition.
Each group’s affairs would be decided according to its own religious tradition
Well read. A model for a plural society.
Newcomers would have no rights
Not quite. The article says: Each group’s affairs would be decided according to its own religious tradition.
questions.rationale: “Issues concerning the different groups domiciled in Madinah would be decided on the basis of their own religious traditions.”

questions.q: What do researchers say happens in the mind when a person faces a crisis?
options: Old habits take over completely
Not quite. The article says: Latent abilities awaken and “brainstorming” produces a superior solution.
Latent abilities awaken and “brainstorming” produces a superior solution
Well reasoned. Difficulties become ladders to success.
Memory improves but thinking stops
Not quite. The article says: Latent abilities awaken and “brainstorming” produces a superior solution.
The mind slows down to protect itself
Not quite. The article says: Latent abilities awaken and “brainstorming” produces a superior solution.
questions.rationale: “When a human being is facing a crisis situation, latent capabilities are aroused which enable him to engage in this process of brainstorming.”
